title: Canary post-decision checklist and incident notifications (working)
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a lightweight, cross-functional checklist and notification templates to be used immediately after a canary decision (promote / hold / rollback) or after an A/B experiment threshold breach. Aim: reduce decision friction, make comms consistent, and ensure operational safety while we iterate on the broader rollout framework.

Scope / audience:
- Audience: PMs, SRE, Observability, Product analytics, Engineering (serving/runtime), Solutions Eng.
- Applies to: short-lived canaries (hours→days), mid-length experiments (up to 2 weeks), and emergency fallback events.
- Not a replacement for the full incident runbook — complements it with rollout-specific steps.

How to use this doc (quick):
1) Triage: confirm the canary decision (promote / hold / rollback) in the rollout dashboard and update experiment record.
2) Run the short checklist below (ops + metrics).
3) Send templated notifications (Slack + email) with links to traces/graphs and action items.
4) If rollback: trigger postmortem cadence and tag incident.

Immediate checklist (first 15 minutes) — owner: on-call SRE + release PM
- Confirm decision and who made it (name + role).
- Snapshot: capture baseline dashboard and canary slice dashboard URLs (attach to experiment).
- Metrics sanity check (quick):
  - Traffic routed to canary slice matches plan (±5%).
  - Latency: p50/p95 within expected delta vs baseline. Quick thresholds: p50_delta < 30ms, p95_delta < 120ms (tunable by product).
  - Error rate (4xx/5xx): relative lift < 0.5% absolute or < 2x baseline (use the stricter rule).
  - Quality signals: rejection-rate / hallucination-rate / rerank-fallbacks — compare to baseline test set.
  - Cost signal: tokens/sec CPU-GPU utilization spike > expected? (flag if >20% vs baseline).
- Observability: ensure logs/trace retention links and span ids are attached.
- Canary health: KV cache hit rate, KV growth, memory pressure, and OOM alarms.
- If any metric crosses the emergency threshold in the 15m window, escalate to incident runbook.

Decision matrix (quick reference) — owner: Release PM / Eng Lead
- Promote if: no threshold breaches in 60m, user-facing quality stable (heuristic), resource utilization within projected bounds.
- Hold (extend canary) if: borderline quality regressions or metrics that need longer signal (e.g., slow drift in rerank quality). Default hold = +24h unless otherwise decided.
- Rollback if: immediate user-impacting regression (error-rate spike), P95 latency > SLA + 200ms for >10m, or memory/OOM trends that threaten nodes.

Escalation criteria (examples):
- Error-rate > 1.0% absolute increase for 10m → page SRE and Eng Lead.
- P95 latency > 500ms and user timeouts increasing → page product on-call.
- Backend token-cost increases >30% and billing alarms triggered → notify finance-signal and product.

Notification templates (Slack first, include channels):
- Slack: #prod-rollouts (threaded)
  "[ACTION] Canary decision: ROLLBACK for release X.Y.Z — initiated by @MayaChen. Reason: p95 latency 620ms (baseline 210ms), error-rate +1.3% absolute. Links: dashboard <url>, traces <url>, jira PROD-421. Immediate owner: @RaviPatel. Next steps: stop routing traffic to canary, run quick root-cause checklist, timeline update in thread."

- Email (if wide impact) — subject: "[Urgent] Canary rollback triggered — release X.Y.Z"
  Body bullet points: one-line summary, key metrics and thresholds, links to dashboards/PR/trace, action owners, ETA for update.

Post-decision 1hr checklist — owner: Release PM + Observability
- Confirm traffic is stable after rollback/promote/hold.
- Run a short smoke test matrix (auth flows, tokenized examples, typical prompt patterns).
- Capture full scoped profiling for the canary nodes (CPU/GPU/IO/NET).
- Tag the experiment with final state (promoted/rolled_back/extended) and close open action items.

24hr follow-up (if not rollback) — owner: Product analytics + Eng
- Check longer latency percentiles and quality signals (rerank, hallucination, automated evals on test suite).
- If show-stopper emerges, execute rollback path.
- If promote: schedule rollout plan (cohort expansion matrix) and update the rollout runway doc.

Rollback script (ops quick steps):
1) Move traffic rule to previous stable version (console toggle or infra script).
2) Confirm no canary instances remain accepting traffic.
3) Run a canary purge on caches if stale results suspected (KV flush note).
4) Post in Slack and open incident ticket with tag "post-canary-rollback".

Comms & postmortem pattern (if rollback happened):
- Rapid postmortem: 48–72h owner: Release PM. Include: timeline, signal graphs, root cause hypothesis, mitigation steps, follow-ups with owners, ticket links.
- Severity classification: follow existing incident policy but use tag "rollout" to aid searchability.
- Optional: customer-facing note if any customers are impacted (coord with CS/legal).

Template: short postmortem headings:
- Summary — what happened in one line.
- Impact — user-facing metrics and duration.
- Detection — how we found it.
- Root cause hypothesis.
- Mitigation and rollback steps executed.
- Action items and owners with due dates.

Monitoring queries / dashboards to link (examples for engineers) — add to experiment record:
- Error rate: sum(rate(api_errors[1m])) by (service)
- Latency: percentile(latency_ms, 95) over service routes
- KV cache hit percent: avg(kv.hit_ratio) over nodes
- Cost: tokens_per_second_by_pool and GPU_utilization_by_node
(Links to exact dashboard panels should be pasted into the experiment ticket.)

Open questions & follow-ups (short):
- Who is the canonical owner for ‘quality signals’ (reenlist analytics or applied-ml)?
- Standardize exact numerical thresholds per product line (we currently use heuristics).
- Automate Slack notifications from the rollout console so manual paste is minimized.
- Should we add a short webhook to create an incident stub automatically on rollback?

Notes from recent run (examples, anonymized):
- 2026-02-20: Canary X triggered hold after p95 latency drift; root cause: unexpected KV growth due to model change. Decision: hold 24h, applied cache-ttl reduction, then promoted. Lessons: add KV growth alerts.
- 2026-01-10: A/B experiment showed small quality regression on unusual prompts; we extended sample size and tuned reranker, then resumed rollout.

Appendix: quick copy-paste Slack snippets
- Promote: "[INFO] Canary promoted to 100% traffic for release X.Y.Z — @MayaChen. Baseline metrics stable; next update in 24h. Dash: <url>"
- Hold: "[INFO] Canary held for +24h — decision by @AnyaKline — reason: slow quality drift on reranker. Owners: @JonasMuller. Dash: <url>"
- Rollback: "[ACTION] Canary rolled back — release X.Y.Z — page SRE and Eng Lead. Follow-up ticket: PROD-421."

Last notes (handy):
- Keep the notification short but include at least one link to a trace and one to the experiment ticket.
- Use the rollout console’s ‘snapshot’ feature before any big change.
- Practice this checklist once per quarter as a tabletop exercise with cross-functional participants.

Unresolved (short-term):
- Automate the decision recording in the experiment DB (owner: Eng infra).
- Define thresholds per product line (owner: Product analytics).

End — please add comments inline and flag anything that should be elevated into the rollout playbook proper."
